messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: continuous-batch latency p95 spike on prod cluster-3 (service=redwood-runtime). Symptoms: queue_depth rising, kvcache.evictions high. Alert: https://alerts.internal/redwood/abc123

jess oncall: Ack — I'm on it. @marco can you grab controller logs and check microbatch sizing?

marco sre: grabbing logs now. Controller shows microbatch_max jumped from 16 -> 64 at 2024-03-03T12:07:21Z. kvcache.evictions=1200 total, rate=45/s. Worker queueing visible on rt-workers-*.

priya runtime: That aligns with the quantized model variant rollout last night. Prefetch heuristics plus aggressive continuous-batching growth can create a prefetch storm and blow out the kvcache under high concurrency.

jess oncall: Customer impact? @sam any flags from CS?

sam custsuccess: CS update: two enterprise tenants reported 10-12s responses, intermittent 502/504 for some requests over the last 20m. Customer A: "major slowdown affecting search features". No billing anomalies yet.

priya runtime: Proposed live mitigation: 1) cap continuous-batch max_microbatch to 16 (was 64) 2) scale back prefetch multiplier to 0.5 3) enable conservative kvcache.eviction_threshold throttle. I can prepare a hotpatch for controller-config.

emily eng: I can push the controller-config change. Plan: run a canary and watch evictions/latency, then roll to 100% if green. Command I propose: `/rollout controller-config cluster=cluster-3 --set microbatch_max=16 --set prefetch_mul=0.5`

jess oncall: Do it. @deploy-bot please start a 10% canary. Keep rollback ready. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Rolling out controller-config to cluster-3 — canary 10% started. Track: https://deploys.internal/roll/xyz789

marco sre: Watching metrics. Canary in — evictions down from 45/s -> ~8/s within 60s. Queue depth decreasing. p95 latency trending down.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity set to S2. Pager suppressed for follow-up with SRE rotation.

jess oncall: Keep canary for 5m then go to 100% if stable.

deploy-bot: Canary stable. Rolling to 100% now.

marco sre: 100% applied. p95 latency returned to baseline (~300-400ms). No new 5xx spikes. kvcache.evictions back to nominal.

priya runtime: Initial root cause hypothesis: prefetch multiplier + microbatch config created larger-than-expected microbatches under high concurrency, exhausting kvcache capacity -> increased evictions -> request queuing -> latency cliff.

jess oncall: Follow-ups: - Priya: permanent fix to prefetch heuristics (PR #3456) - Marco: add kvcache eviction alert and slow-start growth guard for microbatch scaling - Emily: write short runbook entry for emergency cap procedure - Sam: customer comms draft

emily eng: Taking monitoring handoff. I'll watch for 2h and start a postmortem doc: `/docs/incidents/1728005555-contbatch-kvcache`

sam custsuccess: Notified affected customers that mitigation applied and we're doing a root-cause analysis. Will send timeline after postmortem.

jess oncall: Handing off to @emily for follow-up. I'm OOO in 30m. Thanks all.

emily eng: Confirmed hotpatch command used: ```bash
/rollout controller-config cluster=cluster-3 --set microbatch_max=16 --set prefetch_mul=0.5
```

incident-bot: Incident stabilized and closed automatically by auto-escalation rules. Duration: ~27m. Summary: Aggressive continuous-batching growth combined with prefetch storm caused kvcache blowout under high concurrency; mitigated by capping microbatch size and throttling prefetch.

jess oncall: Please add repro steps, telemetry charts (evictions, queue_depth, p95), and exact timestamps to the PM. I'll review first thing tomorrow.

emily eng: Will do. Adding owners and links to the postmortem doc now.

sam custsuccess: Thanks team — customers appreciate the quick response. :white_check_mark:
